title: Truncated Delta-Log-Normal Key-Rank Conjecture
summary: Logarithmic key-rank histograms appear approximately normal in their interior, but whether the full distribution is truncated delta-log-normal remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Establish or refute the conjecture that the side-channel key-rank distribution is a truncated delta-log-normal law: a mixture comprising a point mass at key rank zero and a log-normal component for positive ranks, restricted to the finite rank range imposed by the key space. Although logarithmic key-rank histograms appear approximately normal in their interior, it remains to prove that this full characterization holds or to exhibit evidence that rules it out.

scope.domain: Statistical characterization of side-channel key-rank distributions in symmetric cryptanalysis.
parameters: Key rank: the finite-range random variable whose distribution is being characterized
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove that the full side-channel key-rank distribution has the conjectured truncated delta-log-normal form, or exhibit evidence refuting it.

citations.label: Characterisation and Estimation of the Key Rank Distribution in the Context of Side Channel Evaluations

progress.summary: The source explicitly conjectures a truncated delta-log-normal model based on empirical observations and heuristic support. It provides no general proof or exact characterization.
citation_labels: Daniel P. Martin et al., Characterisation and Estimation of the Key Rank Distribution in the Context of Side Channel Evaluations
